concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of intertriginous wounds, condyloma-like plaques, and granulomatous inflammation, along with elevated flagellins and lack of response to adalimumab, suggest Crohn's Disease.
The patient's symptoms of painful intertriginous wounds, linear moist plaques, and granulomatous inflammation are consistent with Hiddenitis Suppurativa.
The patient's symptoms of granulomatous inflammation and elevated immunoglobulin G antibodies suggest Granulomatous Cheilitis.
The patient's symptoms of painful intertriginous wounds, linear moist plaques, and lack of response to adalimumab suggest Pyoderma Gangrenosum.
The patient's symptoms of elevated immunoglobulin G antibodies, family history of similar condition, and lack of response to adalimumab suggest Autoimmune Enteropathy.
The patient's symptoms of elevated flagellins, granulomatous inflammation, and lack of response to adalimumab suggest Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
